section: Part I, Chapter 3 — Temunah and Tavnit
subtitle: דלאלהֵ אלחאירין — The Guide of the Perplexed
author: Moses Maimonides (1138–1204)
intro: A short lexical chapter. Many assume that temunah and tavnit are synonyms. Maimonides separates them: tavnit, from banah ('to build'), always means a thing's built shape — square, round, triangular — and Scripture pointedly never uses it of God. Temunah, by contrast, is amphibolous (tashkīk): it is said of a sensible shape, of an imagined form, and — its third and highest sense — of the true intelligible notion apprehended by intellect. Only in that third sense is it ever predicated of God. Hover a phrase to see its English light up; tap any word for a gloss; dotted words are key terms.

terms.note: The chapter's pivot. Temunah is said by tashkīk (amphiboly) of three things: (1) the sensible shape of a body, (2) the form held in the imagination after a thing is gone from the senses, and (3) the true intelligible notion grasped by intellect. Only this third sense is ever applied to God — 'and the form (temunat) of the Lord does he behold.'

Derived from banah, 'to build.' It denotes only a thing's built shape — the pattern of the Tabernacle, the form of a bird or a hand. Precisely because it means shape, Scripture never applies it to God in any description.

terms.gloss: amphiboly — predication by gradation, not pure homonymy
terms.note: A single term applied to several things in a primary and derivative way (cf. the mushakkak of chapter 1). Temunah is such a word: said primarily of intelligible form, and only derivatively of sensible or imagined shape — which is why its highest sense can be used of God.

terms.gloss: the imagined form (present in the imagination)
terms.note: The second sense of temunah: the residual image of a thing that the imagination retains once the thing itself is absent from the senses — as in a dream, 'a form was before my eyes,' i.e. an image facing the eyes in sleep.

terms.gloss: the true notion (apprehended by the intellect)
terms.note: The third and highest sense of temunah, and the only one used of God: not a shape of any kind but the true reality grasped by intellect. 'The form of the Lord does he behold' means 'the true reality of God he apprehends.'

aligned.ja: אלג'ז אלאול · אלפצל אלת'אלת' — תמונה ותבנית
aligned.en: Part One · Chapter Three — Temunah and Tavnit

aligned.ja: יט'ן אן מעני תמונה ותבנית פי אללגה אלעבראניה ואחד, וליס כד'לך.
aligned.en: It is supposed that temunah and tavnit have one and the same meaning in the Hebrew language; but it is not so.

pairs.en: It is supposed that temunah and tavnit

but it is not so

aligned.ja: וד'לך אן תבנית הו אסם משתק מן בנה, ומענאה בניהֵ אלשי והיאתה, אעני שכלה, מת'ל אלתרביע ואלתדויר ואלתת'לית' וגירהא מן אלאשכאל.
aligned.en: For tavnit is a noun derived from banah ('to build'), and its meaning is the building of a thing and its configuration — I mean its shape — such as being square, round, triangular, and the other figures.

pairs.ja: וד'לך אן תבנית הו אסם משתק מן בנה
pairs.en: For tavnit is a noun derived from banah ('to build')
and its meaning is the building of a thing and its configuration

aligned.ja: קאל את תבנית המשכן ואת תבנית כל כליו, וקאל כתבניתם אשר אתה מראה בהר, תבנית כל צפור, תבנית יד, תבנית האולם. כל הד'א שכל.
aligned.en: It says, 'the pattern of the tabernacle and the pattern of all its vessels' (Exod 25:9); and it says, 'after their pattern, which thou wast shown on the mount' (Exod 25:40); 'the form of any bird' (Deut 4:17); 'the form of a hand' (Ezek 8:3); 'the pattern of the porch' (1 Chr 28:11). All of this is shape.

aligned.ja: ולד'לך לם תוקע אלעבראניה הד'ה אלאלפאט' פי אוצאף תתעלק באלאלאה בוג'ה.
aligned.en: And therefore the Hebrew language never applies these words to any descriptions pertaining to God in any way.

aligned.ja: אמא תמונה פאנה אסם יקאל עלי ת'לת'ה מעאני בתשכיך.
aligned.en: As for temunah, it is a noun said of three meanings by way of amphiboly (tashkīk).

pairs.en: As for temunah

pairs.ja: פאנה אסם יקאל עלי ת'לת'ה מעאני
pairs.en: it is a noun said of three meanings
by way of amphiboly (tashkīk)

aligned.ja: וד'לך אנה יקאל עלי צורהֵ אלשי אלמדרכה באלחואס כ'ארג' אלד'הן, אעני שכלה ותכ'טיטה, והו קולה ועשיתם פסל תמונת כל וכו', כי לא ראיתם כל תמונה.
aligned.en: Namely: it is said of the form of a thing perceived by the senses outside the mind — I mean its shape and outline — and that is His saying, 'and you make a graven image, the form of anything' (Deut 4:16), and so forth, 'for you saw no form' (Deut 4:15).

pairs.en: Namely: it is said of the form of a thing
perceived by the senses outside the mind
I mean its shape and outline

aligned.ja: ויקאל עלי אלצורה אלכ'יאליה אלמוג'ודה פי אלכ'יאל מן אלשכ'ץ בעד גיבתה ען אלחואס, והו קולה בשעפים מחזיונות לילה וכו', ואכ'ר אלקול: יעמד ולא אכיר מראהו, תמונה לנגד עיני, יעני כ'יאלא בחד'א עיני פי אלנום.
aligned.en: And it is said of the imagined form present in the imagination — that of a person after he has gone from the senses — and that is His saying, 'in thoughts from the visions of the night' (Job 4:13), and so forth, and the end of the passage: 'it stood still, but I could not discern its appearance; a form was before my eyes' (Job 4:16) — meaning an image facing my eyes in sleep.

pairs.en: And it is said of the imagined form

pairs.ja: אלמוג'ודה פי אלכ'יאל מן אלשכ'ץ בעד גיבתה ען אלחואס
pairs.en: present in the imagination — that of a person after he has gone from the senses
and that is His saying, 'in thoughts from the visions of the night'

pairs.ja: יעני כ'יאלא בחד'א עיני פי אלנום

aligned.ja: ויקאל עלי אלמעני אלחקיקי אלמדרך באלעקל. ובחסב הד'א אלמעני אלת'אלת' יקאל פיה תעאלי תמונה, קאל ותמונת י״י יביט, מענאה ושרחה: וחקיקהֵ אללה ידרך.
aligned.en: And it is said of the true notion apprehended by the intellect. It is according to this third meaning that temunah is predicated of Him, may He be exalted: it says, 'and the form of the Lord does he behold' (Num 12:8) — its meaning and explanation being: and the true reality of God he apprehends.
